title: Q1 capacity slices & adaptive scaling framework for reserved GPU pools
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Summary: Deliver a quarterly plan and implementation slices to make reserved GPU pools predictable and cost-efficient for enterprise customers while enabling automatic adaptive scaling. This initiative couples product controls (capacity slices, hedging windows, and policy templates) with runtime capabilities (fast warm path for burst capacity, prioritized KV cache allocation, and graceful fallback routing).

Goals and success metrics:
- KR1: Reduce tail request latency for dedicated pools under burst by 95th percentile <= 120ms for common short-chat workloads (seq<=512) across two pilot customers.
- KR2: Reduce per-token serving cost for dedicated workloads by >=15% through improved batching and prefix caching policies.
- KR3: Implement capacity slices with SLAs that map to customer reservation tiers and demonstrate 99.9% availability for committed throughput over a 30-day window.
- KR4: Ship the autoscale policy editor (console + API) and two durable guardrails (hedged reservations, rapid decommit) with rollout to Pilot Tier accounts.

Planned deliverables this quarter:
1) Product spec for capacity slices & hedging windows (this ticket) with acceptance criteria and rollback plan.
2) Console UX: 'Slice editor' to create reservation slices, attach SLAs, and set autoscale policies.
3) Runtime feature: pre-warm fast-path for reserved bursts + KV cache prioritization for reserved pools.
4) Billing mapping: reconcile usage vs reservation on daily granularity; early-alert KPI for under/over provisioning.
5) Pilot launch with two enterprise customers and post-pilot playbook.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Aggressive pre-warm consumes spare GPU cycles that could otherwise be used for on-demand hosted customers; need hedging thresholds and preemption rules.
- Billing reconciliation complexity (hourly vs daily metering) requires alignment with finance and billing infra (ENG-21001).
- Some older model variants require kernel/quantization paths incompatible with quick warm paths; will build compatibility matrix and fallback route.

Acceptance criteria:
- Capacity slices can be created via API and Console and map to a reservation (unit test + e2e).
- Autoscale policy evaluation runs within request path with <5ms median overhead.
- Two pilot customers onboarded and reporting metrics in the dedicated-console dashboard.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: fragmentation of reserved pools leading to poor utilization. Mitigation: guardrail policies that allow temporary pooling across similar SLA classes and an automated rebalancer (deferred to ENG roadmap).
- Risk: customer confusion around burst allowances. Mitigation: in-console visualizations and default conservative burst budgets.

Next steps:
- Finalize spec and link to engineering tickets for sprint planning (due 2026-01-16).
- Create UX mocks and run quick design review with Solutions (Figma link below).
- Schedule pilot kickoff and legal/finance sync for billing mapping by 2026-02-05.
